cards.explanation: The answer is the prophets. Jesus says, "…everything the prophets have written about the Son of Man will be fulfilled." (Luke 18:31) The prophets were the ones holding the pen, friends. Jesus says what they wrote will be fulfilled.

The answer is mocked and insulted and spit upon, and it's a heavy one. Jesus says, "He will be delivered over to the Gentiles and will be mocked and insulted and spit upon." (Luke 18:32) The Gentiles are the people outside of Israel. I think this part hurts to hear, and Jesus says it plainly anyway.

The answer is True! Jesus says, "They will flog Him and kill Him, and on the third day He will rise again." (Luke 18:33) The hard part comes first, friends, but it isn't the last word. Rising again is the last thing He says in that sentence.

The answer is that the meaning was hidden from them. The text says, "The meaning was hidden from them, and they did not comprehend what He was saying." (Luke 18:34) It doesn't tell us who hid it or why, friends. So we leave it right where the text leaves it.
The answer is begging. The text says the blind man "…was sitting beside the road, begging." (Luke 18:35) He's sitting there asking people for help, friends. That sets up everything he does next.

The answer is that Jesus of Nazareth is passing by. "Jesus of Nazareth is passing by…" the crowd told him. (Luke 18:37) He can't see the crowd, but he can hear it, and now he knows who's in it. Watch what he does with that news, bakers.

The answer is mercy. The blind man calls out, "Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!" (Luke 18:38) He sits there begging, friends, yet the thing he asks Jesus for is mercy. Mercy is the word he uses.

The answer is False! The people leading the way "…admonished him to be silent, but he cried out all the louder, “Son of David, have mercy on me!”" (Luke 18:39) Somebody says hush, and he turns the volume UP. I could never do that, friends. I'd fold like a cookie box in the rain.

The answer is that Jesus stops and has him brought over. "Jesus stopped and directed that the man be brought to Him." (Luke 18:40) Jesus stops, and He wants this man brought to Him. When the man comes near, Jesus asks him a question. It's the one in Luke 18:41.

The answer is "What do you want Me to do for you?" Jesus asks the man this in Luke 18:41. The man had been calling for mercy, friends, and now Jesus asks him straight out. The man gets to say it in his own words.

The answer is True. Jesus says, "Receive your sight!" and then, "Your faith has healed you." (Luke 18:42) Those are His words to the man near Jericho, friends. The man had asked to see again, and that is what happens next (Luke 18:41, 43).

The answer is that he follows Jesus and gives God the glory. The man "…received his sight and followed Jesus, glorifying God." (Luke 18:43) He follows Jesus with his sight back, friends. And he's glorifying God as he goes.
The answer is True! The text says, "And all the people, when they saw it, gave praise to God." (Luke 18:43) The man isn't the only one praising, friends. Everybody who saw it gives praise to God.
